summary: Forest Service steel tower near Wetmore, Alger County: foundations poured by 1934, 107 ft with an enclosed cab in 1955. No source read describes it after 1955.

facts.design: four-leg steel tower with an enclosed observing room at the top, painted orange
facts.status_note: No source read after the 1955 survey says whether the tower still stands
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (per the 1955 survey note)

events.note: Foundations poured by 1 September 1934, per a newspaper item; the completion date is not given in the sources read
Surveyed in 1955 by the Coast and Geodetic Survey, which describes the tower as owned and operated by the Forest Service

evidence.supports: foundations poured for new towers near the Alger County airport, 1934
evidence.quote: The forest service has poured the foundations for new towers near the Alger county airport

evidence.supports: site in the southern end of the Hiawatha National Forest
evidence.quote: in the southern end of the Hiawatha National Forest.

notes_for_editor: Single source family: a Forest Lookouts page quoting a 1 September 1934 Escanaba Daily Press item and a 1955 NGS data sheet. Sah-Archipedia (sah-archipedia.org/buildings/MI-01-AR4) and Peakbagger returned HTTP 403 to both fetch_text and WebFetch, so their claims (CCC built it, still standing, NRHP listing, a 1.2-mile location) are unverified and not used. The 1934 item places it near the Alger County airport; the 1955 note places it one mile south of Wetmore, which may be the same site or not. The 1934 'no cabin' line sits uneasily with the 1955 enclosed observing room; the story says the sources do not settle it. Record height_m 32.6 matches the 107 ft in the NGS note. Record agency and ownership fields are blank or unknown; the NGS note supports the Forest Service.
